title: standardize API rate limit semantics, idempotency, retry-after + streaming stability in OpenAI compat layer
author: Priya Rao
release_notes: Standardize 429/Retry-After semantics, add idempotency dedup cache with consistent 409 handling, improve streaming resume behavior and OpenAI compatibility. Backwards-compatible API changes.
description:
Motivation: Customers integrating via the OpenAI compatibility layer observed inconsistent rate-limit behavior (sometimes missing Retry-After, occasionally HTTP-date vs seconds format), and mismatched error codes for idempotency conflicts vs rate-limit responses. Streaming endpoints could also return truncated events on transient connection resets without a clear resume path. This PR standardizes semantics across the API surface (hosted + compat layer), improves streaming stability, and implements server-side idempotency key dedup semantics.

What this PR does (summary):
- Unify rate-limit handling: translate internal rate-limit headers/counters into OpenAI-compatible 429 responses with a stable JSON error body and a Retry-After header. Retry-After is emitted as seconds when TTL < 48 hours and as an HTTP-date when >48 hours (configurable). Error code exposed is "rate_limit_exceeded".
- Idempotency key handling: middleware persists idempotency keys to the dedup cache with configurable TTL (default 24h). On duplicate create requests we now return 409 with code "idempotency_error" when payload conflicts, and 200 + cached response when identical. This mirrors customer expectations and OpenAI semantics.
- Consistent error mapping: centralize error -> HTTP mapping in api/errors.py so downstream clients using the compat layer receive stable codes and messages (e.g., TooManyRequests -> 429/rate_limit_exceeded, IdempotencyConflict -> 409/idempotency_error, TemporarilyUnavailable -> 503/service_unavailable). Added documentation for clients in docs/openai-compat.md.
- Streaming stability: streaming handler now supports resumable streams using a short-lived resume token returned in the stream metadata on chunk boundaries. On network reset, clients can re-open the stream and provide the token to continue from the last committed token. We also hardened chunk framing so partial frames are buffered and not emitted. Added unit+integration tests that simulate jitter/partial frames.
- Telemetry & observability: added metrics for idempotency cache hit/miss, rate-limit mapped responses, and streaming resume events. Updated tracing tags to include idempotency_key and rate_limit_bucket where available.
- Tests and CI: added unit tests (api/errors, openai_compat middleware), integration tests for streaming resume, and an e2e test exercising OpenAI-compat rate-limits. Addressed a flaky integration test by increasing retry/backoff in the test harness.

Files changed (high-level):
- redwood/openai_compat/middleware.py - new translation layer for rate-limit + idempotency semantics
- api/handlers/streaming.py - stream resume token support and robust chunk framing
- api/errors.py - centralized error->HTTP mapping and stable OpenAI error shapes
- infra/idempotency/cache.py - dedup cache interface + TTL config
- docs/openai-compat.md - updated docs and examples showing Retry-After and idempotency flows
- redwood-sdk-typescript/examples/stream-resume.ts - example of using resume token
- tests/integration/test_streaming_resume.py - simulate network interruptions
- tests/unit/test_error_mapping.py, tests/unit/test_idempotency_cache.py

- b7c9d4e: implement idempotency cache and middleware
- 3d4a5f6: add streaming resume token support and robust framing

- Diego: "Integration tests were flaky on CI; I recommend a deterministic backoff in the test harness." (Request changes)

- Liam: "Approve after minor doc clarifications." (Approved)

CI summary: unit tests: pass, lint: pass, integration: initially failed (network jitter test), rerun integration: pass, e2e: pass (slow). Final CI status: pass.

Manual testing & rollout notes: We feature-flagged the new compat translation behind feature flag 'compat-rate-idempotency-v2'. The rollout plan:
1) Enable for a small percentage of traffic and monitor rate_limit_mapped_count and idempotency_cache_hit_rate.
2) Increase to 100% after 24h stable metrics and no increase in client errors.
3) Remove the legacy code path after one week of successful traffic.

Related/previous PRs: pr-60321-standardize-api-rate-limit-idempotency-retry-after-openai-compat.json, pr-72145-standardize-api-rate-limit-idempotency-retry-after-openai-compat.json

Merge: squash and merge into main. No database migrations. Backwards compatibility: preserved; clients not using idempotency keys see no behavior change.
